column1: What are the three successive phases of the DOM Event Propagation lifecycle in modern browsers?
column2: Capturing phase, Target phase, and Bubbling phase.

column1: In the DOM event lifecycle, which phase travels from the window/document downwards through ancestor nodes to the target element?
column2: The Capturing phase (Trickling phase).

column1: In the DOM event lifecycle, which phase travels upwards from the event target through all ancestor nodes back up to the window/document?
column2: The Bubbling phase.

column1: By default, does addEventListener('click', handler) register its handler for the capturing phase or the bubbling phase?
column2: The bubbling phase (capture is false by default).

column1: How can you register an event listener to run during the capturing phase instead of the bubbling phase?
column2: Pass { capture: true } or true as the third argument to addEventListener().

column1: What is the core architectural principle of Event Delegation in JavaScript?
column2: Attaching a single event listener to a shared parent/root container to handle events triggered by any of its descendants via event bubbling.

column1: What modern DOM method searches up the ancestor chain from an element (including itself) to find the closest ancestor matching a CSS selector?
column2: Element.prototype.closest() (e.g. event.target.closest('[data-action]')).

column1: If no matching ancestor is found when calling element.closest(selector), what value is returned?
column2: null.

column1: Why does Event Delegation consume less browser memory than attaching individual event listeners to 100 separate button elements?
column2: It allocates only 1 event listener object in memory instead of 100 separate listener function instances and binding references.

column1: How does Event Delegation eliminate stale listener bugs when DOM elements are dynamically inserted, filtered, or replaced?
column2: Because the listener resides on the permanent root container, newly rendered children bubble events automatically without needing re-attached listeners.

column1: In an event handler, what is the difference between event.target and event.currentTarget?
column2: event.target is the innermost element that initiated the event, while event.currentTarget is the element to which the event listener is currently attached.

column1: What JavaScript DOM API method prevents the browser's default action (such as following an anchor link or submitting a form) from executing?
column2: event.preventDefault().

column1: What JavaScript DOM API method stops an event from bubbling further up the DOM hierarchy?
column2: event.stopPropagation().

column1: In the WAI-ARIA Tabs pattern, what role must be applied to the container wrapping the selectable tab buttons?
column2: role="tablist".

column1: In the WAI-ARIA Tabs pattern, what role must be applied to each individual filter button?
column2: role="tab".

column1: What is the concept of 'Roving Tabindex' in accessible widget navigation?
column2: Setting tabindex="0" on the currently active tab (making it focusable via Tab key) while setting tabindex="-1" on all inactive tabs (so Tab moves past the group).

column1: In WAI-ARIA tablist navigation, how should a keyboard user navigate between tabs within the tablist?
column2: Using Arrow keys (ArrowRight / ArrowLeft / ArrowDown / ArrowUp) to move focus, while Tab exits the tablist to the next focusable widget.

column1: What ARIA attribute on a tab button points to the ID of the container element whose display it controls?
column2: aria-controls="[target-element-id]" (e.g., aria-controls="portfolio-grid").

column1: Why should focusable child elements (buttons, links) inside hidden cards receive tabindex="-1" when filtered out?
column2: To prevent keyboard users from tabbing into invisible, hidden elements and losing visible focus context.

column1: In the CSS rendering pipeline, why is animating transform and opacity computationally cheaper than animating height or top?
column2: transform and opacity are handled directly on the GPU/Compositor thread without triggering expensive Layout (Reflow) or Paint recalculations.

column1: What happens to a CSS opacity transition if display: none is applied simultaneously on the same element?
column2: The transition is bypassed immediately because display: none instantly removes the element from the browser rendering/layout tree.

column1: What CSS pseudo-class matches an element only when focused via keyboard or non-pointer navigation, preventing focus rings on mouse clicks?
column2: :focus-visible.

column1: In JavaScript, what Set method provides an O(1) membership check to validate if a string exists in a whitelist?
column2: Set.prototype.has() (e.g. VALID_CATEGORIES.has(slug)).

column1: What String method in JavaScript removes leading and trailing whitespace characters?
column2: String.prototype.trim().

column1: In the context of Single-Page Application (SPA) architecture, what is 'Unidirectional State Flow'?
column2: A pattern where state is stored as a single source of truth, user actions update that state, and the UI renders deterministically from the updated state.
